There, she came into contact with American journalist Agnes Smedley along with other progressive figures from China and abroad. Inspired by their influence, Wei resolved to dedicate herself to the Chinese revolution and the cause of the Chinese people's liberation. While her public-facing work involved compiling bibliographies, she was also engaged in clandestine activities behind the scenes. Thus began Wei Lushi's "double life" in Shanghai.
